context: Quarterly platform talk given by Priya Rao, head of engineering at a mid-size software company. Dan is in the audience and listens. Facts from the plan: the migration budget is $1.2 million, the target is 31 July, the old data centre closes on 30 September, the team has 14 engineers.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Good morning everyone, thank you for joining the quarterly platform talk. I will go through where the migration stands, what went wrong, and what we do next.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Let me start with the big picture. Two years ago we ran everything on three machines in one rack, and today most services run on the new container platform.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: The first half of the year was about moving the stateless services. They were the easy part, and we moved forty of them with no customer noticing.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: The second half is about the databases, and here I have to be honest, because we are behind.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: We planned to move the orders database in April and we are now in the middle of a long dry run that shows the copy needs nine hours, not the three we assumed.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Because of that, the cutover will happen over a weekend and we will freeze orders for a short time.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Now the budget. We started with one point two million dollars and I can tell you we have spent about nine hundred thousand of it so far.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: The largest part was the licence for the storage system, and we also paid for two consultants who helped us with the network design.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: A word about observability. We moved from the old metrics tool to an open standard called OpenTelemetry, and every team now sends traces in the same format.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: This took longer than planned, because every team used its own naming for the same thing, and we had to agree on one.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Let me talk about people. We are fourteen engineers and two of them are on leave until August, so the real number for the next two months is twelve.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I am asking each team lead to protect two days a week for migration work, and nothing else may take them.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: There is a risk I want to name. The old data centre contract ends on the thirtieth of September, and there is no extension option.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: If we miss the databases, we will pay for a month of emergency hosting, and that costs about three hundred thousand.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Security is the other area. We replaced shared passwords with short-lived tokens, and every access to production now leaves a record.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: One audit finding remains open, about the old backup tapes, and I will close it when the tapes are destroyed.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Customer impact has been small. We had two incidents this quarter that came from the migration, and both lasted less than twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I want to thank the support team, because they handled every ticket during those incidents without escalating a single one.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Now the plan for next quarter. First, finish the databases by the thirty-first of July. Second, switch off the old load balancers. Third, write the guide for new joiners.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I will share the slides after this session and I will keep the channel open for comments.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Some details on cost per service. The average service now costs us nineteen percent less to run, but the databases cost more, because we pay for replicas in two regions.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: We will review those replicas in the autumn, and if the traffic does not need them, we will drop one region.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: A short story from the weekend dry run. At two in the morning the copy stopped, because a disk filled up, and we learned that nobody had set an alert for it.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: We fixed it in ten minutes, but it is a good example of why the checklist matters.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I will now take a break from slides. Please look at the diagram on the screen, it shows the order of the cutover steps.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Thank you all. If there is anything I missed, please send it to me in writing.
